findings: The strongest retained repository source says only that two unordered linked lists do not intersect structurally and asks how to find nodes whose values are equal; the candidate preserves that distinction and does not reinterpret the prompt as the classic linked-list intersection problem.

The source does not define value type, duplicate behavior, first-vs-all result semantics or API. The candidate labels int values, all matching node pairs, Cartesian duplicate semantics, stable index ordering and null-as-empty as explicit candidate choices rather than source facts.

The hash-index invariant is correct for the chosen API: every right-side position is indexed by value before scanning the left list, so expanding all indexed positions for each left node yields exactly the equal-value node pairs without omitting duplicates.
The complexity claim O(n+m+k) time, O(m) auxiliary indexing space plus O(k) output matches the committed implementation.

The committed Java fixture was independently re-executed with OpenJDK 21 during this review and produced exactly 'PASS fixed=7 randomized=5000 oracle=nested-loop duplicateSemantics=cartesian-pairs order=left-then-right'; fixed cases cover empty inputs, no match, multiple matches, duplicate Cartesian semantics, zero/negative values and disjoint node identities.
The candidate contains multiple source-specific follow-ups, explicitly separates alternative narrower contracts, and does not fabricate production or personal experience.
Formal promotion remains blocked by the repository human-approval gate; this isolated review does not substitute for that approval.
